name: Dot's head
description: Dot's head, drawn on its own and large, to be composed into `ss.char.dot` by `use` at about a fifth of this size. It is built from the skull out. A three-quarter head turned to the viewer — forehead at the upper right, the back of the skull at the left, a jaw that runs from the hinge under the ear down to a chin at the lower right — drawn first in a muted skin, and everything on it shaped to that skull: a close leather coif whose front edge runs from the forehead down the temple to the jaw hinge, seamed and stitched over the crown and held by a chin strap with the one buckle on the whole head; a cloth wrap wound round the lower face along the jaw to the chin, so the chin's line reads through it; a deep wool hood whose opening is cut along the coif's edge and bound in leather, so the face sits framed in it rather than lost in it; a scarf wound twice at the throat under the chin, its tail frayed over the collar. The face shows from the brow to the top of the wrap: the near eye on the cheek turned to the viewer is a full almond with a heavy lid and a lash, the far eye is foreshortened beside the bridge of the nose, the brows taper, the nose is a straight bridge with a shadow on its far side and a nostril at the tip, a cheekbone is lit with a hollow under it, and the temple, the far side and the jaw sit in shadow. A bone bead hangs on a cord from the hood's rim. Two leather grommets at the crown take the feelers — the first inch of each is here; the long dead arcs belong to the character document, where they can be animated.
